faqs.question: Which HGV licence do I need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the vehicle and use: C1 is generally 3.5–7.5 tonnes, C is for rigid goods vehicles above 3.5 tonnes, and C+E is for Category C vehicles towing a trailer over 750kg. We’ll confirm the right route from the intended vehicle’s MAM and your current licence.

faqs.question: What is the difference between C1, C and C+E?
faqs.answer: C1 covers medium vehicles between 3.5 and 7.5 tonnes; Category C covers large rigid goods vehicles; Category C+E adds a trailer over 750kg and is the articulated/Class 1 route.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Class 1 and Class 2?
faqs.answer: Class 1 is the common industry name for Category C+E. Class 2 is the common name for Category C.

faqs.question: Is C+E the same as Class 1?
faqs.answer: Yes. Category C+E is commonly called Class 1.

faqs.question: Is Category C the same as Class 2?
faqs.answer: Yes. Category C is commonly called Class 2.

faqs.question: Can I go straight from a car licence to Class 1?
faqs.answer: Yes. Eligible drivers with a full car licence can follow the C+E Direct route.

faqs.question: Do I have to pass Category C before taking C+E?
faqs.answer: Not for the direct route. We offer C+E Direct from a full car licence. Our standard C+E course is for people who already hold Category C.

faqs.question: Which licence lets me drive a 7.5-tonne vehicle?
faqs.answer: Category C1 is the usual entitlement for a vehicle over 3.5 tonnes and up to 7.5 tonnes MAM.

faqs.question: Which licence do I need to drive a rigid lorry?
faqs.answer: Category C is the normal large-rigid-lorry entitlement. C1 covers medium vehicles up to 7.5 tonnes.

faqs.question: Which licence do I need to drive an articulated lorry?
faqs.answer: Category C+E is the normal entitlement for articulated lorries and other large vehicle-and-trailer combinations.

faqs.question: Which licence do I need for a bus or coach?
faqs.answer: Category D is the full bus and coach category; D1 may cover smaller minibuses. The exact entitlement depends on passenger seats and use.

faqs.question: Does passing C+E automatically give me Category C?

faqs.question: What is a Category C1 licence?
faqs.answer: Category C1 covers vehicles over 3,500kg and up to 7,500kg MAM, with a trailer up to 750kg.

faqs.question: What vehicles can I drive with C1?
faqs.answer: Category C1 covers vehicles over 3,500kg and up to 7,500kg MAM, with a trailer up to 750kg.

faqs.question: How heavy can a C1 vehicle be?
faqs.answer: Up to 7,500kg maximum authorised mass for the C1 vehicle; separate trailer rules apply.

faqs.question: Do I need C1 for my motorhome or campervan?
faqs.answer: A motorhome over 3.5 tonnes and up to 7.5 tonnes normally needs C1; over 7.5 tonnes normally needs Category C. Check the vehicle's plated MAM.

faqs.question: Does C1 include Initial Driver CPC?
faqs.answer: Initial CPC is generally required only when the driving will be professional and no exemption applies. It is package-dependent, not automatic for every C1 candidate.

faqs.question: What is a Category C licence?
faqs.answer: Category C covers large rigid goods vehicles over 3,500kg MAM with a trailer up to 750kg. It is mainly used for rigid vehicles between 7.5 and 32 tonnes.

faqs.question: What vehicles can I drive with Category C?

faqs.question: Is Category C suitable for rigid lorries?

faqs.question: Can I drive a tipper with Category C?

faqs.question: What is a Category C+E licence?

faqs.question: What are all the steps to become an HGV driver?
faqs.answer: Typical first-time route: hold a full car licence; complete a D4 medical; submit D2 and D4 for provisional entitlement; pass Module 1a multiple-choice and 1b hazard perception; pass Module 2 if professional CPC is needed; complete practical training; pass Module 3a off-road and 3b on-road; then pass Module 4 if professional CPC is needed.

faqs.question: What should I do first?
faqs.answer: Choose the vehicle category, then arrange the D4 medical and provisional application. We can help plan the route.

faqs.question: Do I need the medical before applying for provisional entitlement?
faqs.answer: Yes. The D4 medical report is normally submitted with the D2 provisional application.

faqs.question: Can I study for theory while waiting for my licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. We recommend using the waiting time for provisional entitlement to study, although the tests cannot be booked until the provisional licence is available.

faqs.question: How do I apply for provisional HGV entitlement?
faqs.answer: Complete a D2 application and a doctor-completed D4 medical report, then send both with the required licence/documents to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1BR. GOV.UK says there is no application fee.

faqs.question: Will NEDS help me complete the application?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can arrange the medical and help with D2/D4 paperwork.

faqs.question: What are Modules 1a and 1b?
faqs.answer: Module 1a is the vocational multiple-choice theory test; Module 1b is hazard perception.

faqs.question: What is Module 2?
faqs.answer: Module 2 is the Driver CPC case-studies test for new professional drivers.

faqs.question: What is Module 3a?
faqs.answer: Module 3a is the off-road practical exercise/reversing test, including coupling elements for trailer categories.

faqs.question: What is Module 3b?
faqs.answer: Module 3b is the on-road practical driving test with an examiner.

faqs.question: What is Module 4?
faqs.answer: Module 4 is the Driver CPC practical demonstration test covering professional vehicle-safety knowledge; it is not another road-driving test.

faqs.question: In what order do I take the tests?
faqs.answer: Provisional entitlement comes first, followed by Modules 1a and 1b; Module 2 if required; practical training; Modules 3a then 3b; and Module 4 if required. Module 2 must be passed before Module 4 on our training route.

faqs.question: Can I complete everything during one week off work?
faqs.answer: The practical driving block may fit into about one week, but the full medical, provisional, theory and CPC process normally cannot be completed in one week.

faqs.question: Which parts are handled by NEDS and which by DVLA or DVSA?
faqs.answer: We can arrange/support the medical, paperwork, study materials, training and test bookings. DVLA issues provisional/licence entitlements; DVSA controls official theory and on-road tests; authorised our facilities may conduct Module 3a and Module 4.

faqs.question: Can you manage the entire process for me?
faqs.answer: We offer a managed start-to-finish service, subject to external DVLA/DVSA processes.

faqs.question: What happens after I pass?
faqs.answer: DVLA updates the relevant driving entitlement. If full Initial Driver CPC was completed, a DQC is issued for professional driving; periodic training is then required to keep CPC current.

faqs.question: What is Driver CPC?
faqs.answer: Driver CPC is the professional qualification normally required to drive lorries, buses or coaches as the main part of a job.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Initial and periodic CPC?
faqs.answer: Initial CPC is the qualification route for many new professional drivers and includes Module 2 and Module 4 alongside licence tests. Periodic CPC is ongoing training used to keep an existing professional qualification current.

faqs.question: What is a Driver Qualification Card?
faqs.answer: The Driver Qualification Card, or DQC, is evidence of Driver CPC. Professional drivers must carry it when required.

faqs.question: What is Module 2 CPC?
faqs.answer: Module 2 is a computer-based case-studies test for the Initial Driver CPC route.

faqs.question: What is Module 4 CPC?
faqs.answer: Module 4 is a practical demonstration test of professional vehicle-safety knowledge.

faqs.question: Must I pass Module 2 before Module 4?
faqs.answer: Module 2 must be passed before Module 4 on our Initial CPC route.

faqs.question: I will only drive privately—do I need CPC?
faqs.answer: Non-commercial private carriage can be exempt from Driver CPC, but the correct vocational driving entitlement is still required.

faqs.question: How many periodic CPC hours do I need?
faqs.answer: You need 35 hours within each five-year period. For professional driving in Europe all 35 hours must be International Driver CPC; UK-only drivers can use National courses or a mix permitted by GOV.UK.

faqs.question: Which CPC subjects do you offer?
faqs.answer: Our Driver CPC topics include drivers’ hours, working time, tachographs, safe loading, safe and fuel-efficient driving, transport documents, defects and emergency first aid.

faqs.question: How can I check how many CPC hours I already have?
faqs.answer: Use the GOV.UK 'Check your Driver CPC periodic training hours' service. You need your driving-licence number and postcode.

faqs.question: When will I receive my DQC?
faqs.answer: The DQC is normally sent automatically to the address on the driving licence. For periodic training, contact DVSA if it has not arrived within 20 days of when it was due.

faqs.answer: The balance is payable before the relevant practical vehicle training and tests. The exact deadline will be shown on your booking documents.

faqs.question: Do you offer finance?
faqs.answer: We offer staged-payment and direct-debit arrangements. We do not currently advertise a separate third-party credit product, so please ask which payment plan is available.

faqs.question: Can my employer pay?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to us accepting and recording the company booking/payment details.

faqs.question: Can you invoice a company?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can arrange an invoice for a company booking; credit and payment terms must be agreed before booking.

faqs.question: Do you accept card payments?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can pay for selected products or deposits by card through our online shop and payment provider.

faqs.question: Can you price a package for several employees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ask us for a tailored group quotation with dates, delivery location, VAT, travel and certification fees.

faqs.question: Can I reserve a place without paying?
faqs.answer: A deposit is required to reserve a course place. Ask us if a temporary quotation hold is possible.

faqs.question: What information do you need to book me in?
faqs.answer: We need your contact details, course or category, broad current licence status and preferred timeframe. Please use our secure process for licence numbers, identity images or medical details rather than sending them in this chat.

faqs.question: Do you provide weekday training?
faqs.answer: Yes. our course information use weekday practical blocks. Confirm the exact dates for the selected course.

faqs.question: Are Saturday medical appointments available?
faqs.answer: Saturday medical appointments may be available, subject to availability.

faqs.question: Can I change my course dates?
faqs.answer: Please ask us before the course. Amendments may incur an administration charge of up to £50 plus VAT, and any cancellation calculation will use the original start date.

faqs.question: Can I transfer to a different licence category?
faqs.answer: Please ask us before the course. Amendments may incur an administration charge of up to £50 plus VAT, and any cancellation calculation will use the original start date.

faqs.question: Can I transfer my booking to another person?
faqs.answer: For classroom courses, you may be able to nominate a substitute before the course begins. Vehicle-training transfers require our approval.

faqs.question: What happens if I am ill on the training day?
faqs.answer: Contact us immediately. For genuinely unavoidable non-attendance after a course starts, we may sometimes offer alternative dates, but the full fees remain payable.

faqs.question: Can I postpone my training?
faqs.answer: Please ask us before the course. Amendments may incur an administration charge of up to £50 plus VAT, and any cancellation calculation will use the original start date.

faqs.question: Will I receive a refund if DVSA cancels the test?
faqs.answer: DVSA may allow a claim for certain out-of-pocket expenses after a short-notice cancellation. We’ll confirm the effect on your course, replacement test and any vehicle-hire charge.

faqs.question: Do you provide training in Newcastle?
faqs.answer: We provide Gateshead-based training for learners from Newcastle, Sunderland, Durham and the wider North East. We’ll confirm the venue when you book.

faqs.question: Do you provide training in Sunderland?

faqs.question: Do you provide training in Durham?
faqs.answer: We provide Gateshead-based training for learners from Newcastle, Sunderland, Durham and the wider North East. We’ll confirm the venue when you book.

faqs.question: Do you train customers from outside the North East?
faqs.answer: Yes, customers may travel to the centres. Some business training can also be delivered nationwide.

faqs.question: Can you deliver training at our company’s premises?
faqs.answer: We offer client-site and nationwide delivery for suitable business courses. Vehicle/facility requirements and travel costs must be agreed.

faqs.question: Is nationwide training available?
faqs.answer: We offer client-site and nationwide delivery for suitable business courses. Vehicle/facility requirements and travel costs must be agreed.

faqs.question: How do I reach you by public transport?
faqs.answer: The 93 and 94 bus services from Gateshead Interchange run near our Team Valley centre. Please check current timetables before travelling.

faqs.question: Do I need an ADR certificate?
faqs.answer: Drivers carrying dangerous goods above relevant thresholds normally need an ADR card covering the goods carried. Employer/DGSA advice should confirm the exact requirement.

faqs.question: Which ADR course should I take?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether you carry packages or tanks and which dangerous-goods classes are involved. Give us the load type/classes for a tailored route.

faqs.question: What does the Core module cover?
faqs.answer: Core is the mandatory general foundation covering common ADR safety duties before packages/tanks and class-specific modules.

faqs.question: Can I book an individual ADR module?
faqs.answer: Optional class modules can be added, but Core and delivery-mode prerequisites apply. We’ll confirm the valid combination.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail an ADR exam?
faqs.answer: The failed module test must be retaken under the current ADR rules. Ask us for retest timing and fees.

faqs.question: Do you provide ADR refresher training?
faqs.answer: ADR refresher training and exams are the route to stay qualified. Confirm our next refresher course and modules.

faqs.question: Can you provide ADR training for our company?
faqs.answer: We offer business training; ask for a group ADR proposal covering modules, dates and location.

faqs.question: My forklift certificate has expired—do I need a refresher?
faqs.answer: UK forklift certificates do not have a universal statutory expiry date. The employer should assess competence and arrange refresher/retest where needed.

faqs.question: What certificate will I receive?
faqs.answer: Successful operators receive training evidence or certification identifying the truck type and training completed. We’ll confirm the exact certificate or accreditation for your course.

faqs.question: Can you train me on more than one truck type?
faqs.answer: Training should be appropriate to each truck type. We can quote for multiple categories, but separate conversion/additional training may be required.

faqs.question: Can training take place at our workplace?
faqs.answer: Yes. We offer on-site and off-site forklift training, subject to suitable facilities and equipment.

faqs.question: Can you train several employees together?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ask us for a group plan based on truck types, candidate experience and site suitability.

faqs.question: How difficult is the qualification?
faqs.answer: It is an intensive qualification that requires study. Difficulty varies by person, so please review the syllabus and sample material before enrolling.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail an exam?
faqs.answer: The failed exam component must be retaken under the awarding body’s rules. We’ll confirm resit preparation, dates and fees.

faqs.question: Can I visit the centre and look at the materials first?
faqs.answer: Yes. You’re welcome to contact us or arrange a visit to discuss the course and look at the study material.

faqs.question: Can OLAT help after a DVSA investigation or public inquiry?
faqs.answer: OLAT may be used for refresher or remedial needs and to meet Traffic Commissioner requirements. It is training, not legal representation or a guaranteed outcome.

faqs.question: Is OLAT available online?
faqs.answer: We offer online OLAT as well as classroom/nationwide delivery. Confirm current dates and platform.

faqs.question: Can OLAT be delivered at our premises?
faqs.answer: We offer nationwide delivery; client-site suitability and travel costs must be agreed.

faqs.question: Can you deliver training at our depot?
faqs.answer: Yes for suitable courses. We offer client-site and nationwide delivery, subject to site suitability, accreditation and travel arrangements.

faqs.question: Do you provide nationwide business training?
faqs.answer: Yes for suitable courses. We offer client-site and nationwide delivery, subject to site suitability, accreditation and travel arrangements.

faqs.question: Can you arrange medicals for several drivers?
faqs.answer: Yes. We offer driver medicals and business programmes; ask for a group schedule.

faqs.question: Can you monitor employees’ Driver CPC requirements?
faqs.answer: Employers can view a driver's CPC record if the driver creates and shares a temporary password through the GOV.UK service. We can support training planning but should not access records without authority.

faqs.question: Can one person coordinate bookings for our company?
faqs.answer: Please ask us to work with a nominated company contact, subject to appropriate authority and data protection.

faqs.question: Can you provide certificates and attendance records to our business?
faqs.answer: We can provide relevant certificates and attendance evidence. We’ll confirm which records can be released to the employer and obtain any required consent.

faqs.question: Can you provide training required by an insurer or auditor?
faqs.answer: We can tailor competence training and assessments, but the insurer/auditor must confirm the exact evidence it will accept.

faqs.question: Can you make reasonable adjustments?
faqs.answer: DVSA provides reasonable-adjustment routes for tests. We’ll discuss any training-centre or vehicle adjustments with you before booking.

faqs.question: Can I bring an interpreter?
faqs.answer: Foreign-language interpreters are not generally permitted for GB practical tests. BSL/interpreter support may be available for deaf candidates; request it through DVSA and confirm training arrangements with us.

faqs.question: Can I take the theory test with language support?
faqs.answer: The GB theory test is in English or Welsh, with BSL and approved accessibility support. Foreign-language voiceovers are not generally available.

faqs.question: Can I train if I have limited experience driving manual vehicles?
faqs.answer: Our LGV fleet includes manual and automatic vehicles. Ask us which option is suitable and how it affects your entitlement.

faqs.question: Can you help an older driver return to HGV driving?
faqs.answer: Yes. our assessment and driver-development services can be used to identify suitable refresher training, subject to the licence and medical remaining valid.

faqs.question: Can you provide refresher training after a long break?
faqs.answer: Yes. our assessment and driver-development services can be used to identify suitable refresher training, subject to the licence and medical remaining valid.

faqs.question: Can you help me find an HGV job after I pass?
faqs.answer: We are not an employment agency, but it has relationships with local employers and may pass suitable candidate details on when employers are recruiting.

faqs.question: Do you work with local employers?
faqs.answer: Yes. We have relationships with local employers, although vacancies are not guaranteed.

faqs.question: Can you pass my details to recruiting companies?
faqs.answer: We may pass candidate details to recruiting clients, but it should do so only with the candidate's permission.

faqs.question: Do I need to give permission before you share my details?
faqs.answer: Yes. Personal details should not be shared for recruitment without an appropriate lawful basis and clear permission where required.

faqs.question: Should I take ADR to improve my employment prospects?
faqs.answer: ADR can open roles carrying dangerous goods, but it does not guarantee work and should match the jobs you intend to pursue.

faqs.question: Can I start work immediately after passing?
faqs.answer: You need the correct driving entitlement and, for professional work, the required CPC/DQC position. Employers may also require induction, insurance approval and experience.

faqs.question: Do you provide a pass certificate?
faqs.answer: Official test results/pass evidence are provided through the DVSA process. Ask us which course-completion certificates it also supplies.

faqs.question: I want to make a complaint—who should I contact?
faqs.answer: Contact us on 0191 500 9450 or info@nedrivingschool.co.uk with your booking details and a factual account. A person will review and handle your complaint.

faqs.question: I am unhappy with my instructor—what can I do?
faqs.answer: Contact us on 0191 500 9450 or info@nedrivingschool.co.uk with your booking details and a factual account. A person will review your concerns about the instructor.

faqs.question: Will you send me marketing messages?
faqs.answer: Only if you separately opt in. Marketing consent on our contact form is optional.

faqs.question: Can I opt out of marketing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the unsubscribe option in marketing communications or contact us to withdraw marketing consent.

faqs.question: Do you store card details?
faqs.answer: Payment-card details are handled by our payment provider and are not stored by us. Never send card details in this chat.

faqs.question: How can I request a copy of my personal data?
faqs.answer: Contact us using the privacy-policy contact route to exercise data-access, correction or deletion rights. Some records may have to be retained for legal or certification reasons.

faqs.question: How can I correct or delete my information?
faqs.answer: Contact us using the privacy-policy contact route to exercise data-access, correction or deletion rights. Some records may have to be retained for legal or certification reasons.

faqs.question: Can I use my own vehicle for C1 training?
faqs.answer: Possibly - It will have to meet the required standards set by the DVSA and you will have to have the correct insurance policy to allow learner drivers to undertake a driving test. Our team can help advise you.

faqs.question: Can I train using a non-UK driving licence?
faqs.answer: No, you must have a valid UK driving licence and complete a medical to gain provisional before completing any training.

faqs.question: Can I train if I have exchanged a foreign licence?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you have completed an application to exchange your licence to a UK licence, you will be able to complete training.

faqs.question: My vocational entitlement has expired—what do I need to do?
faqs.answer: You will need to complete a driver medical and submit the application forms to regain your licence.

faqs.question: Can I train if I have points on my licence?
faqs.answer: Having 3 to 6 points on your licence is usually fine to complete a provisional application and complete training however providers or employers may review higher points on a case by case basis. The points will carry over to your full licence when passing but they rarely stop you from learning.

faqs.question: Can I train after a driving ban?
faqs.answer: You can complete training to get your licence back as long as you have legally reapplied for a provisional licence and your disqualification period has ended.

faqs.question: I already hold a DQC—do I still need Initial CPC?
faqs.answer: No - Initial CPC is only if you have not completed Driver CPC before, if you already have a Driver Qualification Card and you are needing to renew, you will need to complete 35 hours in the classroom.

faqs.question: I have previously driven HGVs abroad—what route do I need?
faqs.answer: I would recommend applying for a UK driving licence and then completing a driving assessment to access how you drive the larger vehicles, this might minimize your package.

faqs.question: I previously had a DQC—do I need Initial or periodic CPC?
faqs.answer: Periodic CPC

faqs.question: My DQC has expired—what should I do?
faqs.answer: You will need to complete 35 hours Driver CPC training to renew your Driver Qualification Card.

faqs.question: I have a medical condition—can I still obtain an HGV licence?
faqs.answer: You will need to complete a driver medical, and as long as you meet the requirements and your medical condition does not affect your driving, you will still be able to obtain the licence.

faqs.question: I take medication—will it affect my medical?
faqs.answer: Taking medication does not automatically fail your driver medcical but you must declare all regular prescriptions and relevant over the counter medicines to the examining doctor. As long as the medication you take does not affect your driving for example, blurred vision, dizziness, drowsiness or slow reaction time then you should pass.

faqs.question: Can you advise me privately about medical eligibility?
faqs.answer: You must pass a DVLA D4 medical assessment before you can obtain a heavy goods licence.

faqs.question: I am pregnant—can I undertake practical training?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can legally complete HGV training while pregnant provided you have approval from your doctor or midwife and remain comfortable and fit to drive.

faqs.question: I disagree with a test result—can NEDS appeal it?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is an appeals procedure, there will be instructions on how to do this given to you by your examiner along with your result.

faqs.question: What information will the chatbot collect?
faqs.answer: A safe initial enquiry should collect only a name, preferred contact route, phone/email, course of interest, broad licence status and preferred timeframe. It should not collect card, licence-number, identity-document or medical details in ordinary chat.

faqs.question: How will my enquiry information be used?
faqs.answer: This is internal information, this will not be shared or leaked due to GDPR.

faqs.question: Who will my information be shared with?
faqs.answer: Only with staff within the business who will be needing access to your information to complete licence checking or to check relevant documentation before testing.

faqs.question: Can I submit my licence or medical information through chat?
faqs.answer: No. Please do not send a driving-licence number, licence image or medical information in this chat. Use the secure, purpose-specific process we provide.

faqs.question: How can I contact you?
faqs.answer: Please either send us an email or ring our team with the information provided on the NEDS website; you will find our contact details at the bottom of the chatbot and on the top left of our website.
